Test: Apply Grain Transfer, CONNECT A GRAIN SOURCE LAYER, let the FIRST frame render at FULL resolution, then scrub on. Read BOTH logs: GrainTransfer_gpu.log holds the GPU verdict, GrainTransfer_diag.log holds the per-frame cache state.
Expected result / pass criteria: ONE CPU frame, then GPU frames. That first frame pays for the FFT analysis on the CPU and populates the compute cache; only from the second frame can PreRender raise GPU_RENDER_POSSIBLE. If every frame stays on the CPU the cache gate is the first suspect, NOT §2.2 — the opposite diagnosis from the other three. Check the diag log first: hasSource=0 or fullRes=0 means the precondition was never met, which is not a gate bug.

Test: A/B with Preview Grain Only ticked — the isolating view
Expected result / pass criteria: ≤ 1e-5. It renders mid-grey plus the modulated grain field, opaque: exactly the field being added, with no plate underneath to mask a difference.

Test: A/B default params over a real plate
Expected result / pass criteria: max-abs ≤ 1e-5 per channel.

Test: Change the Grain Source layer
Expected result / pass criteria: The cache key changes, so the next frame drops back to CPU for ONE frame, then returns to GPU. That round trip is the gate working. A permanent CPU fallback after a source change is the bug to look for.

Test: Change the Seed
Expected result / pass criteria: Same round trip: one CPU frame, then back to GPU.

Test: Change the project bit depth
Expected result / pass criteria: Same round trip: one CPU frame, then back to GPU.

Test: Render at half, then quarter preview resolution
Expected result / pass criteria: CPU by design — analysis is full-res gated (at half res AE aliases the grain away and the measurement would read content, not grain). CPU here is correct, not a failure.

Test: Determinism: render the SAME frame number on GPU and on CPU, difference them
Expected result / pass criteria: ≤ 1e-5. Grain is re-randomised per frame from (seed, frame), so both paths must produce the same field for the same frame number. This is the real test for this plugin.

Test: Scrub back and forth over a range
Expected result / pass criteria: A frame must not change when revisited.

Test: Amount = 0 on both paths
Expected result / pass criteria: An EXACT passthrough — not merely ≤ 1e-5.

Test: A layer with a soft alpha edge
Expected result / pass criteria: Alpha untouched everywhere; zero-alpha pixels pass through by contract.

Scene-linear / ACES project (LogFromLinear encode) — include superwhite values
Expected result / pass criteria: ≤ 1e-5. This path round-trips through LinToLog/LogToLin and is where an exp2/log2 mismatch between backends would show.

Test: 6K — confirm it still renders
Expected result / pass criteria: Renders. Note this plugin's gate is the analysis cache, not a memory budget, so a TOO BIG line is not the expected decline here.

Expected result / pass criteria: A frame is identical whether reached by scrubbing or by batch render. Watch that the analysis cache survives the MFR workers rather than forcing CPU on every frame.
